source_review.notes: Reviewed the original GK paper/official record, primary KLL and t-digest papers, t-digest size analysis, and current Apache DataSketches quantile/KLL/REQ documentation. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Deterministic, probabilistic, relative-rank, empirical, interpolation, and implementation claims remain assigned to their respective algorithms.

evidence: Checked observation count n, inclusive natural/normalized rank R and r, quantile Q, epsilon, delta, GK tuple fields, KLL k, compactor weights, and centroid terminology.
Checked inclusive, exclusive, nearest-rank, retained-value, and interpolated semantics are distinguished.
Checked absolute rank, relative rank, value, deterministic, probabilistic, and empirical errors are not conflated.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter consistently evaluates formal guarantees in rank space and treats value-space loss separately.

evidence: Recomputed fixture allowance 0.05*200=10 and exhaustive observed maximum error 10 across 101 quantiles.
Recomputed fixture q50, q90, q95, and q99 exact ranks/errors as 110/10, 185/5, 200/10, and 200/2.
Recomputed GK merge examples as 7+8+4=19 <=20 and 12+9+6=27 <=30.
Recomputed exercise allowance 0.002*50000=100 and uniform one-percent versus p99.99 tail ratio as 100.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The finite tuple count and errors characterize one order and epsilon, not worst-case space constants or the general theorem.

evidence: Verified GK lower and upper rank formulas from cumulative gaps and tuple delta.
Verified permitted adjacent GK compression conserves total gap mass and preserves sorted representative order.
Verified pair compaction replaces two weight-w items with one weight-2w item, conserving represented mass.
Verified absolute rank error cannot imply numeric value error without distribution assumptions.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The full GK/KLL space and probability proofs remain attributed to their primary papers.

evidence: Reviewed empty/singleton, exact endpoints, duplicates/plateaus, gaps, monotone/reverse/alternating orders, shard skew, and tail ranks.
Reviewed NaN, infinities, signed zero, locale/cross-language comparators, weights, negative updates, huge weights, and value interpolation.
Reviewed incompatible k/compression/error modes, merge trees, random seeds, repeated compaction, corruption, malformed weights, and serialization.
Reviewed sliding windows, late events, reset generations, concurrent compaction/snapshots, crashes, replay, and exact confirmation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable fixture uses distinct integers and excludes duplicates, floats, weights, merge, randomization, windows, concurrency, persistence, and corruption.

evidence: The bounded GK model processes exactly 200 distinct values and retains 15 sorted tuples.
The sum of tuple gaps is exactly 200 and every interior gap-plus-delta satisfies the final threshold.
All 101 checked normalized quantiles remain within the ten-rank allowance against a fully sorted oracle.
Exact output records q50, q90, q95, and q99 estimates, ranks, and errors.
invariant_checking.notes: A finite invariant pass is evidence for the fixture and implementation path only.

evidence: Reviewed GK proof structure through insertion intervals, compression precondition, cumulative rank bounds, and query selection.
Reviewed KLL mechanism through weighted levels, parity compaction, mass conservation, randomized rank contributions, and capacity schedule.
Reviewed why t-digest centroid size results and empirical tail accuracy are different proof objects.
Reviewed why merge requires algorithm-specific recompression and why insertion-only summaries are not invertible windows.
proof_review.notes: No new full GK/KLL theorem, REQ theorem, t-digest accuracy theorem, weighted algorithm, or concurrent merge proof is claimed.

evidence: The GK and compactor proof obligations are labeled separately from operational recommendations.
The t-digest discussion labels tail accuracy as empirical and does not borrow KLL guarantees.
The executable model explicitly disclaims general proof, merge, weighted, concurrent, and production coverage.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Every selection recommendation names the guarantee domain and evidence type.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact fifteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
Independent arithmetic reproduced all fixture, rank-threshold, tail-ratio, and exercise calculations.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local front-matter, section, local-link, example, exercise, answer, and snippet checks passed before review.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No many-seed KLL coverage test, adversarial-order campaign, t-digest trace study, REQ tail study, weighted summary, merge tree, cross-language serialization, concurrency/crash test, benchmark, or deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter makes rank the formal error domain, connects retained mass to compression correctness, and separates uniform, tail-relative, empirical, and value-relative objectives.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed comparator/item schemas, duplicate/endpoints, NaN/infinity, weights, parameters, randomness, merge trees, envelopes, windows, generations, concurrency, persistence, metrics, tests, migrations, and exact fallbacks.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review establishes rank versus value; the GK model exposes tuple invariants; ten examples cover gaps, compression, median bounds, compaction, tails, duplicates, compatibility, randomness, NaN, and windows; five exercises transfer to migration and payments architecture.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Greenwald, Khanna, Karnin, Lang, Liberty, Dunning, Ertl, Apache, database, data-engineering, observability, concurrency, security, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production GK/KLL/REQ/t-digest implementation, randomized rank coverage, tail/value accuracy, mergeable GK variant, weighted/deletion/window algorithm, compatible cross-language format, concurrent/persistent service, certification, nor deployment fitness.
